$70 cash Aquarian deal; stock ~$41.55 (~68% gross spread) prices high break risk; Dec 6 2026 outside date, regulators (DE/NY/MA) not done, extension talks ongoing -> extension 8-K is the dated asymmetric trigger

verified.catalyst: Barrick Mining is putting its North American gold assets into American Barrick Gold Corp (Nevada Gold Mines share, Pueblo Viejo, Fourmile) and plans to sell a minority stake in an IPO. The registration statement was filed on 10-Nov-2026, and the IPO is meant to show the market what the parts are worth.
verified.dated_milestone: Barrick press release and IPO registration on 10-Nov-2026 (done). Next: the amended filing with a price range, then pricing. Both are undated; management only says late 2026 or early 2027. No firm date exists.
verified.instrument: B (NYSE common, $33.39 on 2026-11-20). The listing of ABGC itself is not yet priced and not tradeable.
verified.bloom_gates: G2 only, and weakly. A registration statement for the IPO is on file, a concrete step. G1 fails: no named buyer or anchor investor, and the underwriters were not verified. G3 fails: there is no price range, IPO size or ABGC valuation, so nothing specific is left unpriced. Triage error: Barrick's release calls the filing an S-1, not an S-11 (the S-11 is a REIT form). The flagged 10-15% stake size is unverified.
verified.edge: L. Run-up from the pre-catalyst base: about -21%, not a run-up. B closed at $42.27 on 9-Nov, the day before the filing announcement, and is $33.39 now (FMP 2026-11-20). That is a 52-week low, against a $54.69 high and a $40.27 50-day average. Remaining % to a favorable resolution: cannot be re-derived. Without a price range or ABGC valuation there is no figure for the parts. Barrick has no preferred stock in front of the common, but selling 10-15% of a subsidiary still leaves about 85-90% inside B. Any re-rating comes from the market multiple put on ABGC, which is judgement plus gold beta, not a contracted amount. The 21% fall since the filing tracks gold and costs, not the event. The IPO did not stop it, so the stock trades on gold.
verified.primary_source: GlobeNewswire, Barrick press release "Barrick Announces American Barrick and S-1 Filing for Proposed Initial Public Offering", 10-Nov-2026. Seeking Alpha, "American Barrick Gold Launches IPO For Separation And Production Growth", 16-Nov-2026. FMP quote and daily price history for B through 2026-11-19/20.
verified.analysis: The event is real, dated and still ahead. Barrick's 10-Nov-2026 release names American Barrick Gold Corp and the IPO filing, and the Q3 call says the IPO is coming. But nothing in it can be priced: no range, no size, no valuation, and pricing is only "late 2026 or early 2027". The sum-of-parts gain cannot be re-derived from the capital structure, so per the numerator rule this scores the equity, not the event, and is capped at 4. The equity is dominated by the gold price (down 21% since the filing, at a 52-week low on cost pressure and gold), which makes this mostly a macro bet. Gap: web search budget was exhausted, so the filing itself, the stake size, the underwriters and the latest 10-Q/40-F debt figures were not read directly. Re-check when an amended filing shows a price range. That is the first point where G3 could pass.

verified.catalyst: Brighthouse and Aquarian must amend the merger agreement before the Dec 6, 2026 outside date. An extension 8-K, followed later by approvals from the DE/NY/MA insurance regulators, would re-rate a stock that prices the $70 cash deal as roughly a 20-25% probability.
verified.dated_milestone: 2026-12-06 outside date (either side can terminate after it). Watch for an extension or termination 8-K before then. Next fixed date is the preferred record date, 2026-12-10, which is not a deal event.
verified.instrument: BHF common (cash deal at $70/sh). The non-cumulative preferreds (BHFAP etc.) are the lower-beta alternative.
verified.bloom_gates: G1: named counterparty (Aquarian Holdings VI L.P., merger agreement dated 2025-11-06). G2: concrete commitment (contractual $70 cash per share, outside date auto-extended 2026-09-06 to 2026-12-06, and both parties say they 'remain committed' and are negotiating a further extension). G3: specific unpriced figure ($70 vs $41.55).
verified.edge: M. Run-up from the pre-announcement base is about -15% to -25%: the stock now trades BELOW where it was before the deal and sits near its 52-week low of $41.01. So nothing is harvested, and the market is actively pricing a break. Remaining from $41.55 to the $70 contractual value is +68.5%. Assuming a break value of about $35, the implied completion probability is about 20%. The edge is real only if Aquarian's financing and regulatory issues are less bad than the tape implies. This is a binary bet with an informed-looking market on the other side, hence M, not H.
verified.primary_source: BHF Form 10-Q for Q3 2026, filed 2026-11-05 (sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1685040/000168504026000037/bhf-20260930.htm), merger note on the Outside Date. FMP quote 2026-11-20 ($41.55). Seeking Alpha 2026-10-06 on financing and regulatory scrutiny.
verified.analysis: The Q3 10-Q (2026-11-05) confirms the outside date auto-extended to 2026-12-06. It also says regulatory approvals are 'not expected to be received in time' and that the parties are discussing an extension, with 'no assurance' they agree. So the deal is live, unfired and contractual (exempt from numerator provenance), and the near-term dated trigger is an extension or termination 8-K within about two weeks. A cash deal price needs no waterfall re-derivation, but the falling price (50-day average $47 to $41.55 now, below the pre-deal level) shows the market treating Aquarian's financing and the regulatory scrutiny (Seeking Alpha, 2026-10-06) as serious break risk. An extension 8-K buys time but not approval, so the asymmetric payoff needs regulatory approval, which is undated. Gap: web search was unavailable (budget exhausted), so I could not check for news after Nov 5 on extension terms, price renegotiation or regulator status, and the pre-deal base price is estimated, not fetched.

verified.catalyst: FDA review of the resubmitted Vyglxia (troriluzole) NDA in spinocerebellar ataxia, with a user-fee goal date in 1Q27. The triage note's PCNS AdCom, whose briefing-document release would be the trade, is not confirmed by any source I could reach and has no date.
verified.dated_milestone: PDUFA goal date in 1Q27; the company has given only the quarter, not a day. The AdCom date and briefing-doc release are unconfirmed and undated. Next checkpoint: an FDA Federal Register AdCom notice, which usually comes 2-8 weeks before the meeting.
verified.bloom_gates: G1 partial: the counterparty (FDA) is named and the resubmission was accepted. G2: there is a 1Q27 PDUFA quarter but no day-level date, and the AdCom is not dated. G3 not met: no specific unpriced figure; approval value sits inside a $2.06B multi-asset pipeline.
verified.edge: L-M. Run-up: the stock was $11.75 on 2026-10-21, the day before the resubmission was accepted. It closed $14.69 on 10-22 (+25%) and is $13.65 now (+16% versus the pre-catalyst base). Remaining: I estimate about +20-30% to roughly $16.5-17.5 on approval, since the 52-week high of $18.24 was set before the earlier rejection. A second rejection probably sends it back to the ~$11 base or lower (about -20% or more). The acceptance re-rating has already been partly harvested. The SCA asset is diluted by other pipeline noise: the opakalim partial clinical hold (Sep 2026), the BHV-1530 cancer-drug data that lifted the stock +8% on 11-19, and the Ono/SK licensing deals. So a briefing-doc move is a smaller share of value than in a single-asset name. Odds of a favourable outcome are not high either: the FDA rejected this drug once before, on a real-world-evidence external-control trial design.
verified.primary_source: Biohaven Q3 2026 results press release, PRNewswire 2026-10-29 (FDA accepted the troriluzole SCA resubmission, PDUFA 1Q27). Barron's/Benzinga 2026-10-22 on the acceptance-day move. FMP EOD prices 2026-10-15 to 10-27 and quote 2026-11-20 ($13.65, market cap $2.06B).
verified.analysis: FMP sources confirm the resubmission was accepted with a 1Q27 goal date (Q3 release 2026-10-29) and the stock's +25% day on 2026-10-22. I could not verify the claimed PCNS AdCom: the shared web-search budget was used up, and no FMP press release or news item mentions an advisory committee, so the briefing_doc lane has no dated trigger. This is a multi-asset equity with no preferred stock ahead of the common, but I did not re-check cash and burn in the 10-Q. A third of the flagged upside is already priced since acceptance, and the PDUFA date is quarter-only. WATCH at score 4: upgrade if an FDA Federal Register notice dates the PCNS meeting, which would make the briefing-doc release (two business days before the meeting) a dated catalyst.
